message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling on a PJ Masks Owlette infant costume. A footed jumpsuit plus headpiece would be a festive-article costume under 9505.90.6000 if it is not a wearing apparel set. However, CBP has often classified costumes made of textile as 9505 only when they are not ordinary apparel. For infant sizes, a jumpsuit that is a "romper" type might be classified in 6111. But the item is a costume with a character headpiece, and CBP usually treats such costumes as festive articles in 9505.90.6000 (other festive, carnival or other entertainment articles). Note that Chapter 95 excludes fancy dress of textiles in Chapter 61 or 62 (Note 1(e)), though, which are classified as wearing apparel. In practice, though, CBP rulings treat costumes of flimsy construction as 9505, whereas well-made ones go in 6111. The mention of an infant footed jumpsuit suggests a classification in 6111 or 9505. The headpiece is likely a character hood or mask, making this a set. Under GRI 3(b), the essential character would be the jumpsuit, which would give 6111.30.5020 (infant garments of synthetic fibers, other, other). Still, I think the ruling probably chose 9505.90.6000, since the costume is of flimsy construction and not suited to ordinary wear.
